verdicts.support: the objective of the proposed review is to investigate the effects of chronic exercise on overall depression severity and on different symptoms of depression in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) including older adults ... and by considering the moderating effects of intervention characteristics and individual characteristics
to our knowledge, there is no published review or meta-analysis that attempts to uncover the effects of chronic exercise on the broadest possible range of symptoms as described in the DSM
verdicts.attack: Leaving out 'as described in the DSM' narrows rather than widens the claim.

verdicts.reason: Protocol type and PRISMA-P are quoted.
verdicts.support: we have outlined a protocol for a systematic and meta-analytical review; follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocol (PRISMA-P) statement
verdicts.attack: The RCT and older-adult scope comes from the introduction quote.

verdicts.reason: Only parallel-group design is quoted; cluster designs are not.

verdicts.support: The following electronic databases will be searched from inception
Two independent reviewers will conduct the study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment.

verdicts.reason: Model, effect size and tools are quoted.
verdicts.support: a random-effects model will be used; Summary effects will be calculated as Hedges’ g; rate the quality of the included studies with ROB2; The GRADE framework will be used to assess the evidence accumulated for each outcome
verdicts.attack: Saying GRADE 'assesses quality' is a loose but fair rendering of assessing the evidence.

verdicts.reason: It being a protocol is quoted, but no quote states that it reports no results.

verdicts.support: we expect to find a moderate effect of exercise on depression compared to active and passive control groups with no exercise components; We further expect the results to be moderated by intervention characteristics and individual characteristics
verdicts.attack: Leaving out 'with no exercise components' does not change the claim.

verdicts.reason: Directly stated, with the hedge kept.
verdicts.support: the conclusions drawn from this review may serve as a basis for developing evidence-based recommendations for individualized exercise programs
the review results may reveal research gaps that can stimulate the formulation of research questions for further RCTs

We plan to exclude RCTs with tested effects of pharmacological treatment and / or psychotherapy. Therefore, no conclusions can be drawn for exercise interventions as add-on treatment. ... we might miss some clinically relevant insights.
We further anticipate limitations in form of heterogenous data and a wide variance in the reporting of the exercise characteristics (e.g., detailedness) and the individual characteristics.
it can reveal whether certain moderator variables, such as comorbidities or physical fitness level still require further research
verdicts.attack: 'May' softens 'can', so it is not stronger.
